question.worked_solution:
If we let $u=\frac{2\pi x}{3},$ then

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=\frac{2\pi }{3}\,⟹\,\text{d}x=\frac{3}{2\pi }\text{d}u.
$$

Calculating the limits for $u$ gives

| $x$ | $0$ | $1/2$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $u$ | $0$ | $\pi /3$ |

Using the above, we can write the integral in terms of $u$ and evaluate:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1/2}6\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{2\pi x}{3})\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /3}6\operatorname{cos}⁡u\cdot \frac{3}{2\pi }\,\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{9}{\pi }{\int }_{0}^{\pi /3}\operatorname{cos}⁡u\,\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{9}{\pi }\operatorname{sin}⁡u{|}_{0}^{\pi /3} \\  & =\frac{9}{\pi }(\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{3})-\operatorname{sin}⁡(0)) \\  & =\frac{9}{\pi }(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}-0) \\  & =\frac{9\sqrt{3}}{2\pi }\end{aligned}
$$
